subject: Staff Ops Radar: OKR checkpoints, QBR prep, and tactical asks
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, maya_srinivasan@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai, markus_klein@redwood.ai
Cc: executive-distro@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: Staff Ops Radar: OKR checkpoints, QBR prep, and tactical asks

Team —

Quick weekly radar ahead of next week’s QBR prep window. I kept this tight; please read and flag anything that needs escalation.

Wins
- Dedicated capacity pilot (EU cluster) reached 90% availability during resync stress test; observed 12% improvement in median p99 under burst loads. Ops: thanks @Markus for the tuning.
- Two mid-market customers (Acme Cloud, TeraHealth) signed POCs for model variants; early telemetry shows latency improvements with new KV-cache heuristics.

Risks / Near-term signals
- Support tickets for long-tail inference errors increased 22% Y/Y; root cause points to a regression in kernel selection when sequence-length > 6k tokens. Engineering has a patch but it requires a staged rollout to avoid perf regressions.
- QBR narrative for cost-per-ppm needs an updated runbook. Finance asked for per-route delta by EOD Wednesday; I don’t have that granularity yet.

Asks (action + owner + due)
1) Engineering: approve staged kernel-rollout plan and canary policy by Tue COB — owner: Markus K.
2) Product + Pricing: provide per-route unit-cost delta and summary paragraph for SLT by Wed 11/18 5pm — owner: Monica P.
3) Sales: confirm top-5 expansion opportunities and expected ARR impact for QBR slides — owner: Laura B. (Laura, put placeholders if need be)
4) All: please review the attached QBR_prep_deck_v1.pptx and add comments on slide notes; especially numbers and risk language.

Operational notes
- I’ll run a 20-minute sync tomorrow 9:00am PT to go through blockers; calendar invite sent. If you can’t make it, please leave a comment on the deck or reply to this thread.

Attachments: QBR_prep_deck_v1.pptx, OKR_pipeline_snapshot.csv

Thanks —
Marcus Lin
Head of Platform Ops
Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0186
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: maya_srinivasan@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai, markus_klein@redwood.ai, executive-distro@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 09:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Staff Ops Radar: OKR checkpoints, QBR prep, and tactical asks

Marcus —

Thanks for the concise callout. Quick notes:
- Sales will populate ARR placeholders by EOD Monday; I’ll push the list of top-5 and expected timelines into the slide notes.
- For Finance, suggest Monica borrow the per-route export from usage-analytics (I’ll loop in Jordan if you want a hand).

One ask: can we soften the public-facing risk phrasing around the kernel regression? We should call it "investigation ongoing; staged mitigation planned" rather than "regression" until we have the root cause confirmed.

See you on tomorrow’s sync —
Laura
VP, Revenue Operations
laura.bennett@redwood.ai | ext. 421

Subject: Re: Staff Ops Radar: OKR checkpoints, QBR prep, and tactical asks

Marcus / team —

Two quick items from Product / OKR perspective:
- On the kernel-selection risk: we need a short rollback plan if canary shows increased p99 in a specific region; recommend we preserve the previous kernel image in the EU pool and keep traffic-splitting at 5/95 for 48 hours. I can own validation tests and the rollback playbook.
- OKR check: Pipeline health metric ("serveable-models-at-99p") slipped 3 points this sprint because of longer model-conversion times; I’ve updated the OKR tracker and added a short note on mitigations. See the OKR_pipeline_snapshot.csv for the delta.

Ask: Monica — can you prioritize the per-route unit-cost export to include 90/95/99 percentiles for token costs? Finance specifically asked for distribution not just averages.

Also tagging Acme Cloud contact for the QBR case study: Julie, appreciate any short bullet points you can share about performance improvements you observed during POC (can be internal-only).

—Maya
Director, Product Management
maya.srinivasan@redwood.ai

Appreciate the quick replies and the tactical guidance. A couple of follow-ups and assignments: 

- Markus: please post the staged-rollout doc to the QBR folder and tag it JIRA-4567; keep canary at 5% traffic for 24 hours, then 20% if metrics hold. If canary moves p99 > 10% we roll back immediately.
- Monica: prioritize the per-route percentiles for the cost export; if finance needs interim numbers, use medians plus note on distribution.
- Laura: thanks — placeholders are fine for slides. Please include the 3 prioritized logos for expansion.

I’ve attached an updated deck (QBR_prep_deck_v1.pptx -> QBR_prep_deck_v1a.pptx) with softer risk language and suggested speaking points (slide 6). Also added a short appendix with telemetry snapshots.

Link to folder: https://drive.redwood.example.com/drive/folders/QBR-2026-Prep
JIRA: JIRA-4567 (kernel-rollout)

If there are no objections I’ll mark these as accepted actions and close the loop in the shared tracker by EOD Monday.

Thanks —
Marcus
Head of Platform Ops
Redwood Inference
